To provide operational and service excellence, innovation, community engagement and 
observance of good financial management and accountability. This is in agreement with the 
Republican Constitution (Amendment) Act No.2 of 2016 Part IX on the System of Devolved

Chirundu District Council plans to employ the strategies incorporated in the Intergrated 
Develpoment Plan (IDP) as well as the 8NDP cluster(s) that is accelerating the enforcement of 
the Decentralization Policy and community participation in service delivery and local governance 
though skills development and training in addition to library services and hightened literacy 
levels in the district. The Counicl willl ensure the facilitation of micro, small and medium 
enterprises development, as well as enhancing provision of adequate safe and clean water and 
sanitation in addition to promotion of urban and peri-urban economies through the provision of 
an enabling environment for trade and commerce, by improving market spaces and bus 
stationa, and the maintenance of township roads.

has been allocated to community capital projects while the remaining allocation will be shared

towards legislative functions. 
Integrated Development Planning has a total allocation of K3.8 million of which social economic 
planning has an allocation of K2.9 million for the developmental planning of the District, 
administrative operations and dealing with cross-cutting issues. While, environmental planning 
has been allocated K840,408.
Economic and Business Development comprising of Local Economic Development (Trade 
Facilitation and Licensing) and infrastructural developmental programmes has been allocated 
K1.1 million.
The programme total of K9.8 million for Management and Support Services comprises an 
allocation of K4.9 million for Executive Management which deals with the operations of the office 
of the Mayor and the Town Clerk. K4.2 million allocated to Financial Management - Accounting 
and Valuation for administrative operations which includes resource mobilisation, Debt 
Servicing, Information Communication Technology. While K0.4 million has been allocated for 
Citizen Engagement. The allocation of K190,530 will cater for Procurement of required 
materials, services and equipment. K2,890 allocated to Internal Audit for monitoring of Council 
projects and administrative operations and K1,000 allocated to Public Relations for 
dissemination of information on Council operations and administrative operations.
